name: Hagia Sophia
description: Patriarchal cathedral of the Byzantine capital; converted into the premier imperial mosque in 1453 without a change of name.

name: Topkapi Palace (New Palace)
description: Begun in 1459 and completed in 1478 on the ancient acropolis; became the seat of the Ottoman court.

name: Fatih Mosque complex (site of the Church of the Holy Apostles)
description: Mehmed II's complex; foundation inscription dated 1463-70; eight madrasas; built on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles.

name: Old Palace site (Beyazit)
description: First Ottoman palace in the city near the old Forum of Theodosius (Beyazit Square area). Exact footprint not mapped here.

name: Blachernae quarter and palace area
description: Northern sector where the defence relied on a later single-wall extension; Byzantine imperial residence area. One of the two points where the defence cracked on 29 May.

name: Eyup Sultan complex
description: Shrine associated with the discovery of the tomb of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari after the conquest; outside the walls on the Golden Horn.

name: Galata (Genoese Pera)
description: Genoese colony across the Golden Horn; stayed neutral during the siege. Marker placed on Galata Tower as a landmark for the district.

name: Seraglio Point (Sarayburnu)
description: Headland where the Marmara and Golden Horn walls meet; site later chosen for the Topkapi Palace.

name: Golden Gate and Yedikule Fortress
description: Ceremonial gate at the Marmara end of the land walls; the Ottomans built Yedikule Fortress behind it in 1458.

name: First Military Gate
description: Southern end of the land walls near the Sea of Marmara.

name: Silivrikapi (Gate of the Spring)
description: Gate whose towers carry a 1439 repair inscription in published descriptions.

name: Fourth Military Gate (centre of the Mesoteichion)
description: Described as lying at the centre of the Mesoteichion (Lycus valley) - the sector described as the weakest section of the wall. Ottoman heavy guns were concentrated against the Lycus valley.

name: Gate of St. Romanus (Topkapi)
description: Janissaries breached the stockade near this gate on 29 May. Identification of the gate is debated in the literature; position is approximate.

name: Gate of Charisius (Edirnekapi)
description: Reported command point of Constantine XI in 1453 and, in some accounts, the gate of Mehmed II's entry.

name: Kerkoporta (postern near Blachernae)
description: Small postern that the Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium says was left unattended; exact location is debated, so treat this marker as indicative only.

name: Mal Tepe (traditional command position of Mehmed II)
description: Tradition places the sultan's command position on the mound outside the Topkapi gate. Tradition only; coordinates indicative.

name: Rumeli Hisari
description: Ottoman fortress built 15 April-31 August 1452 at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus (about 660 m).

name: Anadolu Hisari
description: Fortress on the Asian shore built by Bayezid I in 1393-94, opposite Rumeli Hisari.

name: Golden Horn boom (chain)
description: Chain stretched across the mouth of the Golden Horn between Constantinople and Galata (from 2 April 1453). Anchor points are debated; marker is the midpoint of a schematic line.

name: Ottoman fleet anchorage (Dolmabahce-Besiktas shore)
description: Bosphorus shore where the ships hauled overland on 22 April are usually placed. Indicative.

name: Overland landing on the Golden Horn (Kasimpasa shore)
description: Approximate point where the hauled ships entered the Golden Horn behind Galata. The exact route is debated.

name: Golden Horn (Halic)
description: Inlet along the northern side of the city; the sea walls here were single-line and weaker than the land walls.

name: Bosphorus
description: Strait linking the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara; Ottoman control of the shores in 1452 cut the Black Sea route.

name: Sea of Marmara
description: Southern sea approach; the Marmara sea walls were a single line.
